match.reason: No bank point teaches the reasons Australians move within the country, such as work, study, retirement and sea or tree change; the closest, geo-internal-international-migration, only defines internal and international migration, and the mining card covers just one cause.

draft.title: Internal migration in Australia
card: Internal migration is movement within a country. In Australia, people move between cities, towns and regions without crossing a border.
Many people move for work or study. A job offer, or a university or TAFE place, can draw people to a different city or town. Others move to retire, or for the lifestyle.
a move from a big city to the coast, for the beach and a slower pace of life.
a move from a big city to the country, for open space and a rural way of life.
draft.remember: Australians move within the country for work, study, retirement and lifestyle.

a.q: Jo leaves Sydney to live in a small coastal town for a slower pace of life. What is this kind of move called?
opts: A sea change
A tree change
A forced move
An international move
a.why: Jo moves from a big city to the coast for lifestyle, which is a sea change. A tree change is a move to the country, not the coast.
a.clue: Where is Jo moving to: the coast or the country?

b.q: Sam leaves Melbourne for a farming town. He wants open space and a rural way of life, and he has no new job lined up. Which best describes his move?
opts: A tree change, which is internal migration
A sea change, which is internal migration
A tree change, which is international migration
A sea change, which is international migration
b.why: Sam moves from a big city to the country for lifestyle, so it is a tree change. He stays in Australia, so it is internal migration. A sea change would be a move to the coast.
b.clue: Check both where he is going and whether he crosses a border.

b.best: A tree change, which is internal migration

problems.detail: 'without crossing a border' could suggest that interstate moves (e.g. Sydney to Melbourne, which crosses a state border) are not internal migration. It should say 'without crossing a national border' or 'without leaving the country'.

The first card line defines internal migration, a term taught in point 2 (Types of migration), instead of only mentioning it. Question b also tests point 2's distinction between internal and international migration.

proposal.title: Internal migration in Australia
card: Many Australians move from one city, town or region to another without leaving the country. These moves are a form of internal migration.
Many people move for work or study. A job offer, or a university or TAFE place, can draw people to a different city or town. Others move when they retire, or for the lifestyle.
a move from a big city to the coast, for the beach and a slower pace of life.
a move from a big city to the country, for open space and a rural way of life.
proposal.remember: Australians move around their own country for work, study, retirement and lifestyle, such as a sea change or a tree change.
